pairs.prompt: Which opening is more effective for a speech about food deserts?

options.text: "Today I'm going to talk to you about food deserts."
options.feedback: This announces the topic but does nothing to earn attention. The textbook treats getting attention as the first job of an introduction.

options.text: "For Maria, the closest place to buy a fresh tomato is a 45-minute bus ride away."
options.feedback: A brief narrative puts a human face on the issue immediately. Follow it with your topic and a credibility statement.

pairs.prompt: Which opening is more effective for a speech on sleep?

options.text: "Raise your hand if you got eight hours of sleep last night. Keep it up if you did that every night this week."
options.feedback: Audience participation makes the topic personal. Plan how you'll transition if very few hands go up.
Dictionary openings are predictable. A definition can help later in the body if listeners need it.

pairs.prompt: Which opening is more appropriate for a tribute to a retiring custodian?

options.text: A shocking statistic about workplace injuries.
options.feedback: A startling statistic can work in persuasive speeches, but it mismatches a celebration's tone.

options.text: A short story about the morning he fixed the gym lock in the snow so the team could practice.
options.feedback: A specific, warm story fits the occasion and shows his character (Chapter 15).

options.text: "What would you do if your phone was the only record of every photo of your family?"
options.feedback: Specific and personal, so listeners can imagine an answer. It leads naturally to a speech about data backup.

elements.label: Get the audience's attention
elements.help: A story, startling fact, rhetorical question, quotation, reference to the audience, current event, or historical reference.

elements.label: Establish or enhance your credibility
elements.help: Why should they listen to you on this topic? Experience, research, or personal connection.

elements.label: Establish rapport
elements.help: Why does this matter to this audience?

elements.label: Preview your topic, purpose, or central idea
